subject: Feature prioritization: KMS BYOK, retention windows, and SSO questions for Acme Health POC
messages:
From: Lina Morales <security@acmehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-09-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: Feature clarifications: KMS BYOK, retention windows, and SSO for healthcare POC

Jordan —

Thanks again for yesterday's call. As we prepare to move the POC forward there are a few security/compliance items that need clarification before our legal and procurement teams sign off. Can you confirm whether Redwood can meet the following for the Acme Health POC?

- BYOK/KMS: Can customers provide their own keys (KMS) and have keys managed in our cloud KMS (we use AWS KMS) while ensuring Redwood never has persistently decryptable keys? Any doc or integration spec would help.
- Audit logs: We need immutable, exportable audit logs for all API calls and admin console changes with at least 90 days retention — what format and delivery options are available?
- Data retention & deletions: For PII-containing inputs, can you support per-customer retention windows and a guaranteed deletion API that includes confirmation?
- SSO: We plan to use Okta — what's the SAML/SCIM support level and expected setup lead time?

Procurement is also asking whether any of these items require product changes or are covered by configuration/ops. If product work is required, they want an estimate of effort and whether it will block the POC schedule.

Appreciate a concise list of what is out-of-the-box vs what needs engineering.

Best,
Lina Morales
Senior InfoSec Manager
Acme Health

P.S. we can sign an NDA/POC addendum quickly if that helps unblock anything.

I'll follow up with a short note and attach any internal docs.

-Jordan

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-14T15:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Feature clarifications: KMS BYOK, retention windows, and SSO for healthcare POC

Team —

Triage notes (short) below. I tried to separate current capabilities from items that require product/infra changes.

1) BYOK / KMS - Current: We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS for model encryption-at-rest where keys are customer-owned; Redwood does not store plaintext keys. We also support envelope encryption patterns that keep the customer KMS as the root of trust.
- Caveat: For some hosted features (e.g., cross-request caching across workers), we currently rely on a short-term in-memory wrapping key; to fully avoid any transient server-side decryptability we need a small infra change to persist wrappers in a customer-owned KMS path and update KV cache semantics. Estimated infra effort: 2 dev-weeks + 1 security review.

2) Audit logs - Current: Audit events (API calls, admin console actions) are already emitted to an internal event pipeline and can be exported to S3/CloudWatch. Default retention is 30 days for the hosted plan.
- Required for Acme: immutable export with 90-day retention. Ops can configure export to a customer-owned S3 bucket (recommended for immutability) and set lifecycle rules. Product change required? Minimal — we need an admin UI toggle and per-account retention metadata (approx 1 sprint for UI + 1 infra change to store retention policy).

3) Data retention & deletion API - Current: We have an account-level delete endpoint for stored artifacts but no per-customer variable retention windows exposed in the console.
- Product ask: add per-customer retention window configuration (UI + API) and a deletion confirmation webhook. Estimated product + eng scope: 2–3 sprints for a standard implementation (includes testing, documentation, and regression evals). For POC: we can accept a manual ticket-based deletion and provide signed confirmation export within 3 business days.

4) SSO (Okta) - Current: SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported; typical setup is 2–5 business days. For enterprise with custom SCIM claims we have a small config step. Mina can confirm the runbook.

Attachments: I exported a short integration spec (kms-integration-spec.pdf) and an example export manifest for audit logs.

Risk notes:
- Fully BYOK with zero transient decryptability is achievable but requires the infra change above; protecting the KV cache semantics is the main effort.
- Per-customer retention increases metadata surface area and needs thorough QA to avoid accidental cross-account retention misconfig.

Recommended path for POC (minimal blocker):
- Accept operational workarounds for audit log export (customer S3) and manual deletion confirmations.
- Parallel-track infra/product work for BYOK KV cache change and per-customer retention; aim to deliver an MVP within 6 weeks.

Neha
Neha Kapoor
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: kms-integration-spec.pdf (stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-15T10:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Feature clarifications: KMS BYOK, retention windows, and SSO for healthcare POC

Thanks Neha — good breakdown. From a product prioritization perspective here's a pragmatic proposal so we can keep Acme moving without derailing broader roadmap commitments:

Proposal (POC path + follow-on roadmap):
- Short-term (POC, non-blocking):
  - Audit logs: set up export to customer S3 and provide a signed CSV report weekly. (Ops-run, 2 days to configure)
  - Deletion confirmations: manual ticketing with signed export within 3 business days (Ops SLA)
  - SSO: Mina to accept standard Okta flow and test in staging (2–3 business days)
- Medium-term (MVP, 4–6 weeks):
  - Per-customer retention toggle (UI + API) — scope for a single retention policy per account rather than multiple tiers.
  - KMS: limited infra change to store wrapping metadata in customer-keyed path to remove persistent decryptability for stored KV cache wrappers (2 dev-weeks).
- Long-term (quarterly roadmap):
  - Full BYOK guarantee with no transient decryptability across all runtime components; integrate with HSM-backed workflows and update customer SLA.

Ask from engineering for medium-term: 2 backend devs (4 weeks), 1 frontend (2 weeks), and 1 security review. If we can commit those resources we can ship the MVP in ~6 weeks.

I'll prepare a short PRD with acceptance criteria and share the internal link. Jordan — can you confirm Acme's target go/no-go date so we can align?

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Group Product Manager, Security Features
Redwood Inference

Related doc: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/security/ACME_POC_README
